function.name: generate_sea_foam
function.description: Simulates the creation of sea foam based on the agitation level of water, amount of organic material, and the presence of salt. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

agitation_level.description: The level of agitation in the water, represented by a scale from 1 (calm) to 10 (very agitated).

organic_material.description: The amount of organic material present in grams per liter. This is a float type value.

salt_presence.description: Indicates whether salt is present (true) or not (false) in the water.

temperature.description: The water temperature in degrees Celsius. If unspecified, defaults to average sea temperature. This is a float type value.

message.content:
The color of the sea isn’t fixed—it shifts with a mix of physical, chemical, and biological factors:

| Factor | How it changes the color |
|--------|--------------------------|
| **Depth** | Shallow water reflects more of the sky, often giving a turquoise or pale‑blue hue. Deeper water absorbs more light, making it appear darker blue or even black. |
| **Water clarity** | Clear water lets sunlight penetrate deeper, producing a bright blue. Turbid or muddy water scatters light, turning the sea greenish‑brown or gray. |
| **Algae & phytoplankton** | High concentrations of green algae give the water a green tint; certain blooms can even make it appear reddish or brownish. |
| **Sun angle & time of day** | Early morning or late afternoon light can cast a golden or pink glow on the surface. Noon sunlight tends to highlight the blue. |
| **Atmospheric conditions** | Overcast skies reduce the intensity of blue, while clear skies enhance it. |
| **Sediment & organic material** | Suspended sediments or decaying organic matter can tint the water brown or yellow. |
| **Salt concentration** | While salt itself doesn’t color the water, high salinity can affect the refractive index slightly, subtly influencing how light is scattered. |

So, while the “classic” image of the sea is a deep blue, its actual color is a dynamic blend of these influences—ranging from turquoise and green to gray, brown, or even reddish under special circumstances.
